audit.title: CCIP Best Practices (TON)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Sections open with self-contained claims: "Every TON CCIP receiver must implement three mandatory protocol steps in order" and "`MIN_VALUE` is the minimum GRAM your receiver requires attached to each `Receiver_CCIPReceive` message." Lifted chunks stand alone.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good hierarchy (27 headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips, no section over 600 words per measured facts), but 0 tables where the EVM/TON `gasLimit` distinction begs for one, and duplicate H2 "Monitor your dApps" (appears twice) plus generic tail sections harm chunk disambiguation.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong. 0.02/0.03/0.1/0.5 GRAM thresholds, `100_000` gas units, `200_000_000n` nanoGRAM, 10% buffer, 5–15 minute delivery window. Note: measured "version strings [0.02…0.5]" and "GRAM never assigned" are false positives (GRAM amounts and a currency unit), not defects.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good. 3 primary-source GitHub links (Starter Kit, `helper-config.ts`, `utils.ts`), CCIP Directory and Explorer links. Could add a link to TON/Tolk language docs and the FeeQuoter concept page.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. `MIN_VALUE`, `extraArgs`, and the `sender`/`CrossChainAddress` definitions are crisp and near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, `inLanguage` absent, no `datePublished`/`dateModified`, 0 og/twitter tags. Body carries "Last Updated: 2026-04-07" but it is not in machine-readable head. This is the largest scoring drag; note the CLI could not capture `<head>`, so confirm before assuming total absence.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Mixed. TypeScript/bash blocks are labeled with filenames and copy-pasteable; the Tolk snippets are fragments (`assert(...)` lines) with no contract scaffold or imports (measured: 1 import-needing block shows none), and 1 block is untagged.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good lifecycle coverage (implement → configure → fee → monitor → secure), but no error-string or "how do I fix…" headings. Failure symptoms live in body text/CAUTIONs, losing symptom-phrased retrieval.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong. GRAM/nanoGRAM used consistently; entity names (`Router_CCIPReceiveConfirm`, `Any2TVMMessage`) stable. Only minor drag: duplicate section titles and vague "some/most."

audit.summary: This is a well-structured, specifics-dense best-practices page for TON CCIP receivers, with strong answer-first section leads and concrete GRAM/nanoGRAM figures that generative engines can lift verbatim. Its two biggest opportunities are (1) missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no `<head>` dates captured) and (2) the absence of symptom/error-phrased headings that agents actually query by — the page describes "message stuck in-progress," `LowValue`, and `Unauthorized` failures only inside prose and CAUTION callouts. A comparison table for the EVM-vs-TON `gasLimit` semantics would also convert an easily-confused distinction into an extractable unit. Honest verdict: solid Good, held back by metadata and query-coverage gaps rather than content quality.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased headings for the failure modes
recommendations.where: New H3s under "Set `MIN_VALUE` correctly" and a new "Troubleshooting" section.
recommendations.issue: Failures described only as prose: "the message is left in an in-progress state… it cannot be retried."
recommendations.change: Add headings phrased as queries: "Why is my CCIP message stuck in an in-progress state?", "Receiver reverts with `LowValue` / `Unauthorized`", "Message not retriable after out-of-gas". Answer in the first sentence under each.
recommendations.why: Agents query by error string and symptom; concept-titled prose loses retrieval the page already answers verbatim.

recommendations.title: Emit machine-readable metadata
recommendations.issue: Measured — 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified`, `inLanguage` absent.
recommendations.change: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2026-04-07`, `inLanguage: en`, `programmingLanguage: [Tolk, TypeScript]`, and a self-referential canonical URL.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-trust and citation eligibility for agents.

recommendations.title: Add an EVM-vs-TON `gasLimit` comparison table
recommendations.issue: The nanoGRAM-vs-gas-units distinction is spread across two subsections plus a CAUTION; measured 0 tables.
recommendations.change: Add a 2-row table: destination | `gasLimit` unit | helper | default | refund behavior (`buildExtraArgsForEVM`, gas units, `100_000`, no refund vs `buildExtraArgsForTON`, nanoGRAM, `100_000_000n`/0.1 GRAM, surplus returned).
recommendations.why: Engines extract *reasons* from tables; a single unit is the most-confused fact and priors will otherwise default to EVM gas semantics.

recommendations.title: De-duplicate and consolidate the tail sections
recommendations.where: "Monitor your dApps" (H2 appears twice); generic "Evaluate…/Review…/Soak test…" boilerplate.
recommendations.issue: Two identical H2 titles fragment retrieval and dilute the detailed TON monitoring section.
recommendations.change: Rename the second generic "Monitor your dApps" to "General monitoring guidance" or merge into the detailed section; keep one canonical monitoring anchor.
recommendations.why: Duplicate headings break chunk-to-anchor mapping and split ranking signal.

recommendations.title: Give the Tolk snippets minimal runnable context
recommendations.where: Step 1–3 Tolk blocks under "Implement all three mandatory receiver protocol steps".
recommendations.issue: Fragments like `assert(in.senderAddress == st.router)…` with no surrounding handler; 1 untagged block; measured import-needing block shows none.
recommendations.change: Wrap the three asserts in a short `Receiver_CCIPReceive` handler stub showing `st.router`, `MIN_VALUE`, and message context; tag the untagged fence with `tolk`.
recommendations.why: Agents copy runnable units; disconnected asserts can't be assembled without inference.

recommendations.title: Name the tempting-wrong pattern as an explicit Don't
recommendations.issue: "Source chain validation is not enforced at the protocol level on TON" — correct, but relies on the reader inferring the action.
recommendations.change: Add a one-line "Don't assume the Router validates source/sender for you — it does not on TON; check `sourceChainSelector` and `sender` in your handler."
recommendations.why: Skimmed/unretrieved answers default to the EVM idiom where some checks feel implicit; an explicit Don't blocks that substitution.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with numbers where known
recommendations.change: Where a benchmark exists, cite it (e.g., "covers a simple store-and-emit receive at ~X nanoGRAM"); otherwise leave as-is.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation rate.

antiPatterns: Duplicate H2 "Monitor your dApps" (two sections with the same title) — hurts chunk disambiguation.
Generic boilerplate tail sections ("Evaluate the security…", "Review and audit…", "Soak test…") are thin and near-identical to other chains' pages; not stuffing, but low-signal chunks.
One untagged code fence; Tolk snippets lack surrounding context/imports.
No keyword stuffing or marketing fluff detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good; ensure this URL is listed there.
`<head>` metadata could not be captured by the crawler; pass raw `<head>` in the CLI to confirm whether canonical/JSON-LD are truly absent vs unrendered before treating dimension 6 as fully failing.
Site-level freshness cadence and third-party/earned citations (e.g., TON ecosystem docs linking here) are off-page levers that would raise retrieval authority.
